patch_description: Expert insight on Heilbronn-type problems: the objective is bottleneck-driven — the minimum-area triangle improves only when its three vertices are moved to increase that specific triangle's area while not collapsing another. Pure random single-point moves waste most proposals. A directed move strategy that (a) identifies the current minimum triangle, and (b) moves one of its vertices along the direction that increases that triangle's altitude (perpendicular to the opposite edge, away from it), drastically improves proposal quality. Additionally, the 0.67→0.71 results show that multi-restart from the best configuration (basin hopping) is highly effective: local optima for n=13 are numerous and shallow. Finally, since the score is the ratio min_area/hull_area, shrinking the hull can raise the ratio — so after optimization we apply a cheap affine "shrink-to-hull" rescale: translate points so the centroid of the hull is at origin, then isotropically rescale by a factor slightly less than 1 and re-evaluate, keeping the rescaling only if it improves the exact score (deterministic line search). This exploits the fact that any convex rescaling of a valid configuration is still valid, and can turn a plateau in min-area into a gain in the normalized score.
